{{Short description|Canadian biologist}}
'''Bruce Bagemihl''' (1962-)<ref>{{cite web |title=Bagemihl, Bruce, 1962- |url=https://viaf.org/en/viaf/164487356}}</ref> is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[linguist]] and [[cognitive scientist]], and author of the book ''[[Biological Exuberance|Biological Exuberance: Animal Homosexuality and Natural Diversity]]''.<ref name="mcdonald2006">{{cite news|last = McDonald|first = Maggie|date = January 4, 2006|accessdate = March 10, 2018|work = [[New Scientist]]|url = https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg18925332.200-biological-exuberance-by-bruce-bagemihl.html|title = Biological Exuberance by Bruce Bagemihl}}</ref><ref name="fletcher2007">{{cite news|last = Fletcher|first = Martin|date = January 3, 2007|newspaper = [[The Times]]|url-status = dead|url = http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/life_and_style/article1288633.ece|title = Birds do it, bees do it ...|archive-date = February 17, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070217061246/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/life_and_style/article1288633.ece}}</ref>

==Life and career==
He completed a BA at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] in 1981,<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Bagemihl |first=Bruce |url=https://open.library.ubc.ca/soa/cIRcle/collections/ubctheses/831/items/1.0097954 |title=Alternate phonologies and morphologies |publisher=[[University of British Columbia]] |year=1988 |location=University of British Columbia Library |language=en |doi=10.14288/1.0097954}}</ref> and served on the faculty of the [[University of British Columbia]], where he taught linguistics and cognitive science.<ref name="catdir.loc">{{cite web|title=Publisher-supplied biographical information about contributor(s) for Biological exuberance : animal homosexuality and natural diversity / Bruce Bagemihl; illustrated by John Megahan|url=http://catdir.loc.gov/catdir/bios/hol054/98028528.html|website=catdir.loc.gov|publisher=Library of Congress|accessdate=18 September 2017}}</ref> He completed a PhD at UBC in linguistics in 1988, with a dissertation entitled ''Alternate phonologies and morphologies''.

''Biological Exuberance'' cites numerous studies on more than 450 species (see [[List of animals displaying homosexual behavior]]) showing that [[homosexual]] and [[bisexual]] behaviors are common among animals and proposes a theory of sexual behavior in which [[reproduction]] is only one of its principal [[Function (biology)|biological functions]].<ref name = Harrold1999>{{cite news|last = Harrold|first = Max|date = February 16, 1999|title = Creature Comforts|newspaper = [[The Advocate (LGBT magazine)|The Advocate]]|accessdate = March 10, 2018|pages = 61–62|issue = 779|publisher = [[Here Publishing]]|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=aGMEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA61|quote = In his news book, ''Biological Exuberance: Animal Homosexuality and Natural Diversity'' ... author Bruce Bagemihl portrays an animal kingdom that embraces a whole spectrum of sexual orientations ... [and] a complex mosaic that resembles humanity ... 'It's an expanded vision of what the natural world is all about,' [Bagemihl] says.  'We're not alone in having a range of sexual behaviours.  This is something that is all-encompassing.' ... Bagemihl says he didn't write the book because of his own sexual identity. "I'm a scientist who is gay," he says. "I can't separate the two. I wrote this as a scientist, but the implications for humans are enormous." Surprisingly, many of these findings existed when he began to research the book ten years ago...At 751 pages and with photos and documentation of homosexual behaviour in more than 450 species of mammals, birds, repties, and insects, ''Biological Exuberance'' brings the dusty facts to light as Bagemihl deconstructs the all-heterosexual Noah's Ark we've been sold.  ...  Although he doesn't claim to know the motivations of animals, Bagemihl says he does know procreation is not always the driving force: 'Same-sex couplings occur in the presence of the opposite sex, and in and out of captivity, and in and out of mating season.'}}</ref> Bagemihl proposes that group cohesion and lessening of tensions, seen for example among [[bonobo]]s, are other important functions of sexual behavior.<ref name = Kluger1999>{{cite news|last = Kluger|first = Jeffrey|authorlink = Jeffrey Kluger|date = April 26, 1999|url = https://time.com/archive/6735212/the-gay-side-of-nature/ |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080222042308/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,990813,00.html|url-status = dead|archive-date = February 22, 2008|title = The Gay Side of Nature|newspaper = [[Time (magazine)|Time]]|accessdate = March 10, 2018}}</ref>  He also argues that the implications for humans of homosexual behaviour across the animal kingdom are "enormous."<ref name = Harrold1999 /><ref name = Kluger1999 />

His book on homosexuality in animals was cited by the [[American Psychiatric Association]] and other groups in their ''[[amici curiae]]'' brief to the [[United States Supreme Court]] in ''[[Lawrence v. Texas]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.apa.org/about/offices/ogc/amicus/lawrence.pdf|title = Brief for Amici Curiae in Support of Petitioners in the case of ''John Geddes Lawrence and Tyron Garner v. State of Texas''|author1 = American Psychological Association|author2 = American Psychiatric Association|author3 = National Association of Social Workers|author4 = Texas Chapter of the National Association of Social Workers|authorlink1 = American Psychological Association|authorlink2 = American Psychiatric Association|authorlink3 = National Association of Social Workers|authorlink4 = National Association of Social Workers#Chapters|date = January 2003|accessdate = March 10, 2018}}</ref> the case which ultimately struck down [[sodomy laws]] across the United States.<ref name="Love That Dare Not Squeak">{{cite news
 | last = Smith
 | first = Dinitia
 | authorlink = Dinitia Smith
 | title = Love That Dare Not Squeak Its Name
 | newspaper = [[The New York Times]]
 | date = February 7, 2004
 | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2004/02/07/arts/love-that-dare-not-squeak-its-name.html
 | accessdate = April 8, 2023}}</ref> The book formed the basis for the museum exhibition [[Against Nature?]].<ref name="Love That Dare Not Squeak"/>

He has also published several essays and scientific articles on issues related to language, biology, gender, and sexuality.<ref name="catdir.loc"/>

== Selected publications ==

* Bruce Bagemihl. 1988. The morphology and phonology of Katajjait (Inuit throat games). ''Canadian Journal of Linguistics/Revue canadienne de linguistique'' 33(1), 1-58.
* Bruce Bagemihl. 1999. ''Biological Exuberance: Animal Homosexuality and Natural Diversity.'' St. Martin’s Press.
* Bruce Bagemihl. 2001. Animals Do Do It. ''Alternatives Journal'' 27(3), 36.
